newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait arrests five after attack on MP.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait arrests five after attack on MP.

text.p: Kuwait said on Sunday five people, including two Iranians, had been arrested in connection with an attempt to kill a leading liberal opposition parliamentarian.
The Interior Ministry said in a statement the five were transferred to the prosecution for further interrogation ahead of presenting them to justice. It gave no further details.

Gunmen ambushed Oxford-educated Abdullah al-Naibari, 61, on Friday evening as he drove to Kuwait City from a beach near the southern border with Saudi Arabia. He was hit in the jaw and shoulder and his wife suffered a superficial bullet wound near her left shoulder.
Sea captain Abdul-Rahman al-Naibari told Reuters on Sunday that his brother was in "very good condition" in hospital. "He is talking and we read him the newspapers."

Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, who visited Naibari on Saturday, ordered that he be sent abroad for treatment and the Ministry of Health was making arrangements for him to leave by the end of the week.

Political and diplomatic sources said one of those arrested appeared to be a Kuwaiti national who was the target of several recent reports by Talea weekly, the mouthpiece of Naibari's political grouping.
"Talea has reported on many alleged wrong-doings in the past few months, attacking various personalities and groups. They have made quite a few enemies," said a European diplomat.
MPs have accused what they call "public funds thieves" of being behind the attack.
"The main suspect in question now is said to have been a middleman for government contracts. He had a few dealings with arms deals," said a Western diplomat.

In December Kuwait said it had eliminated middlemen from arms purchases to cut costs. MPs have criticised large commissions for brokers in multi-billion-dollar arms deals and have opened several inquiries into alleged irregularities.
Naibari has played a key role in efforts to combat alleged corruption since parliament was restored in 1992 and he often questions lucrative arms deals.
